symbols.name: cubicnl
symbols.summary: Cubic nonlinearity distortion. `cubicnl` is a standard Faust function.

params.name: drive
params.description: distortion amount, between 0 and 1

params.name: offset
params.description: constant added before nonlinearity to give even harmonics. Note: offset can introduce a nonzero mean - feed cubicnl output to dcblocker to remove this.

symbols.name: gate_mono
symbols.summary: Mono signal gate. `gate_mono` is a standard Faust function.

params.name: thresh
params.description: dB level threshold above which gate opens (e.g., -60 dB)

params.name: att
params.description: attack time = time constant (sec) for gate to open (e.g., 0.0001 s = 0.1 ms)

params.name: hold
params.description: hold time = time (sec) gate stays open after signal level < thresh (e.g., 0.1 s)

params.name: rel
params.description: release time = time constant (sec) for gate to close (e.g., 0.020 s = 20 ms)

symbols.name: gate_stereo
symbols.summary: Stereo signal gates. `gate_stereo` is a standard Faust function.

params.name: thresh
params.description: dB level threshold above which gate opens (e.g., -60 dB)

params.name: att
params.description: attack time = time constant (sec) for gate to open (e.g., 0.0001 s = 0.1 ms)

params.name: hold
params.description: hold time = time (sec) gate stays open after signal level < thresh (e.g., 0.1 s)

params.name: rel
params.description: release time = time constant (sec) for gate to close (e.g., 0.020 s = 20 ms)

symbols.name: fibonacci
symbols.summary: Fibonacci system where the current output is the current input plus the sum of the previous N outputs.

params.name: N
params.description: the Fibonacci system's order, where 2 is standard

symbols.testCode:
ef = library("misceffects.lib");
fibonacci_test = 0 : ef.fibonacci(2);

symbols.name: fibonacciGeneral
symbols.summary: Fibonacci system with customizable coefficients. The order of the system is inferred from the number of coefficients.

params.name: wave

symbols.testCode:
ef = library("misceffects.lib");
fibonacciGeneral_test = 0 : ef.fibonacciGeneral(waveform{2, 3});

symbols.name: fibonacciSeq
symbols.summary: First N numbers of the Fibonacci sequence [1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, ...] as parallel channels.

params.name: N
params.description: The number of Fibonacci numbers to generate as channels.

symbols.testCode:
ef = library("misceffects.lib");
fibonacciSeq_test = ef.fibonacciSeq(5);

symbols.name: speakerbp
symbols.summary: Dirt-simple speaker simulator (overall bandpass eq with observed roll-offs above and below the passband). `speakerbp` is a standard Faust function. Low-frequency speaker model = +12 dB/octave slope breaking to flat near f1. Implemented using two dc blockers in series. High-frequency model = -24 dB/octave slope implemented using a fourth-order Butterworth lowpass.

params.name: f1
params.description: low-frequency break point in Hz for the speaker model

params.name: f2
params.description: high-frequency lowpass cutoff in Hz for the speaker model

symbols.name: piano_dispersion_filter
symbols.summary: Piano dispersion allpass filter in closed form.

params.name: M
params.description: number of first-order allpass sections (compile-time only) Keep below 20. 8 is typical for medium-sized piano strings.

params.name: B
params.description: string inharmonicity coefficient (0.0001 is typical)

params.name: f0
params.description: fundamental frequency in Hz

references: "Dispersion Modeling in Waveguide Piano Synthesis Using Tunable
Allpass Filters", by Jukka Rauhala and Vesa Valimaki, DAFX-2006, pp. 71-76

symbols.name: dryWetMixer
symbols.summary: Linear dry-wet mixer for an N-inputs, N-outputs effect. The dry and wet gains sum to 1 for all positions, so this mixer is mono-safe but not constant-power: total power dips at the midpoint (each channel at −6 dB). * `wetAmount = 0`  : dry = 1.0 (0 dB),  wet = 0 * `wetAmount = 0.5`: dry = 0.5 (−6 dB), wet = 0.5 (−6 dB) * `wetAmount = 1`  : dry = 0,           wet = 1.0 (0 dB)

params.name: wetAmount
params.description: the wet amount (0-1). 0 produces only the dry signal at unity, and 1 produces only the wet signal at unity

params.name: FX
params.description: an arbitrary effect (N inputs and N outputs) to apply to the input bus

symbols.name: dryWetMixerConstantPower
symbols.summary: Constant-power dry-wet mixer for an N-inputs, N-outputs effect. The dry input is scaled by cos(θ)/√2 and the wet output by sin(θ)/√2, where θ = π*wetAmount/2. * `wetAmount = 0`  : dry = 1/√2 ≈ 0.707 (−3 dB), wet = 0 * `wetAmount = 0.5`: dry = 0.5 (−6 dB),          wet = 0.5 (−6 dB) * `wetAmount = 1`  : dry = 0,                    wet = 1/√2 ≈ 0.707 (−3 dB)

params.name: wetAmount
params.description: the wet amount (0-1). 0 produces only the dry signal at −3 dB and 1 produces only the wet signal at −3 dB

params.name: FX
params.description: an arbitrary effect (N inputs and N outputs) to apply to the input bus

symbols.name: mixLinearClamp
symbols.summary: Linear mixer for `N` buses, each with `C` channels. The output will be a sum of 2 buses determined by the mixing index `mix`. 0 produces the first bus, 1 produces the second, and so on. `mix` is clamped automatically. For example, `mixLinearClamp(4, 1, 1)` will weight its 4 inputs by `(0, 1, 0, 0)`. Similarly, `mixLinearClamp(4, 1, 1.1)` will weight its 4 inputs by `(0,.9,.1,0)`.

params.name: N
params.description: the number of input buses

params.name: C
params.description: the number of channels in each bus

params.name: mix
params.description: the mixing index, continuous in [0;N-1].

symbols.testCode:
ef = library("misceffects.lib");
mixLinearClamp_test = (1,0,0,0) : ef.mixLinearClamp(4, 1, 1.2);

symbols.name: mixLinearLoop
symbols.summary: Linear mixer for `N` buses, each with `C` channels. Refer to `mixLinearClamp`. `mix` will loop for multiples of `N`. For example, `mixLinearLoop(4, 1, 0)` has the same effect as `mixLinearLoop(4, 1, -4)` and `mixLinearLoop(4, 1, 4)`.

params.name: N
params.description: the number of input buses

params.name: C
params.description: the number of channels in each bus

params.name: mix
params.description: the mixing index (N-1) selects the last bus, and 0 or N selects the 0th bus.

symbols.testCode:
ef = library("misceffects.lib");
mixLinearLoop_test = (1,0,0,0) : ef.mixLinearLoop(4, 1, -0.3);

symbols.name: mixPowerClamp
symbols.summary: Constant-power mixer for `N` buses, each with `C` channels. The output will be a sum of 2 buses determined by the mixing index `mix`. 0 produces the first bus, 1 produces the second, and so on. `mix` is clamped automatically. `mixPowerClamp(4, 1, 1)` will weight its 4 inputs by `(0, 1./sqrt(2), 0, 0)`. Similarly, `mixPowerClamp(4, 1, 1.5)` will weight its 4 inputs by `(0,.5,.5,0)`.

params.name: N
params.description: the number of input buses

params.name: C
params.description: the number of channels in each bus

params.name: mix
params.description: the mixing index, continuous in [0;N-1].

symbols.testCode:
ef = library("misceffects.lib");
mixPowerClamp_test = (1,0,0,0) : ef.mixPowerClamp(4, 1, 1.5);

symbols.name: mixPowerLoop
symbols.summary: Constant-power mixer for `N` buses, each with `C` channels. Refer to `mixPowerClamp`. `mix` will loop for multiples of `N`. For example, `mixPowerLoop(4, 1, 0)` has the same effect as `mixPowerLoop(4, 1, -4)` and `mixPowerLoop(4, 1, 4)`.

params.name: N
params.description: the number of input buses

params.name: C
params.description: the number of channels in each bus

params.name: mix
params.description: the mixing index (N-1) selects the last bus, and 0 or N selects the 0th bus.

symbols.testCode:
ef = library("misceffects.lib");
mixPowerLoop_test = (1,0,0,0) : ef.mixPowerLoop(4, 1, -0.5);

symbols.name: tapeStop
symbols.summary: A tape-stop effect, like putting a finger on a vinyl record player.
symbols.usage: _,_ : tapeStop(2, LAGRANGE_ORDER, MAX_TIME_SAMP, crossfade, gainAlpha, stopAlpha, stopTime, stop) : _,_ _ : tapeStop(1, LAGRANGE_ORDER, MAX_TIME_SAMP, crossfade, gainAlpha, stopAlpha, stopTime, stop) : _

params.name: C
params.description: The number of input and output channels.

params.name: LAGRANGE_ORDER
params.description: The order of the Lagrange interpolation on the delay line. [2-3] recommended.

params.name: MAX_TIME_SAMP
params.description: Maximum stop time in samples

params.name: crossfade
params.description: A crossfade in samples to apply when resuming normal playback. Crossfade is not applied during the enabling of the tape-stop.

params.name: gainAlpha
params.description: During the tape-stop, lower alpha stays louder longer. Safe values are in the range [.01,2].

params.name: stopAlpha
params.description: `stopAlpha==1` represents a linear deceleration (constant force). `stopAlpha<1` represents an initially weaker, then stronger force. `stopAlpha>1` represents an initially stronger, then weaker force. Safe values are in the range [.01,2].

params.name: stopTime
params.description: Desired duration of the stop time, in samples.

params.name: stop
params.description: When `stop` becomes positive, the tape-stop effect will start. When `stop` becomes zero, normal audio will resume via crossfade.

io.raw: _,_ : tapeStop(2, LAGRANGE_ORDER, MAX_TIME_SAMP, crossfade, gainAlpha, stopAlpha, stopTime, stop) : _,_ _ : tapeStop(1, LAGRANGE_ORDER, MAX_TIME_SAMP, crossfade, gainAlpha, stopAlpha, stopTime, stop) : _

symbols.name: transpose
symbols.summary: A simple pitch shifter based on 2 delay lines. `transpose` is a standard Faust function.

params.name: w
params.description: the window length (samples)

params.name: x
params.description: crossfade duration duration (samples)

params.name: s
params.description: shift (semitones)

symbols.name: doppler_shift
symbols.summary: Pitch shifter for signals with known fundamental frequency. Uses Doppler effect from a continuously ramping delay line, with phase-coherent phasor reset synced to the signal period. Best suited for harmonic/periodic signals like oscillator outputs.

params.name: freq
params.description: fundamental frequency of the input signal (Hz)

params.name: ratio
params.description: pitch ratio (1.0 = no shift, 2.0 = octave up, 0.5 = octave down)
